title: OSHA crane power line safety practice questions
description: Free OSHA crane power line safety practice questions on 29 CFR 1926.1408. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Under 1926.1408(a)(1), when the employer identifies the work zone by demarcating boundaries, what else must the employer do?

options.A: Send a copy of the boundary map to the utility owner/operator
options.B: Prohibit the operator from operating the equipment past those boundaries
options.C: Mark the boundaries in red paint on the power line poles
options.D: Repeat the demarcation at the start of every lift

questions.explanation: Under (a)(1)(i) the employer may identify the work zone by "Demarcating boundaries (such as with flags, or a device such as a range limit device or range control warning device) and prohibiting the operator from operating the equipment past those boundaries".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1926.1408(a) require the employer to identify the work zone and make the power line determination?

options.A: Within two working days after operations begin
options.B: After the first load has been lifted
options.C: Only when the operator asks for it
options.D: Before beginning equipment operations

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a) begins: "Before beginning equipment operations, the employer must: (1) Identify the work zone" and (2) make the power line determination.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1408(a)(1)(ii), how may the employer define the work zone instead of demarcating boundaries?

options.A: As the area 360 degrees around the equipment, up to the equipment's maximum working radius
options.B: As the area directly beneath the nearest power line
options.C: As the area the utility owner/operator shows on its service map
options.D: As the area inside the operator's line of sight from the cab

questions.explanation: The second way is "Defining the work zone as the area 360 degrees around the equipment, up to the equipment's maximum working radius."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Option (1) of 1926.1408(a)(2), what must the employer confirm from the utility owner/operator?

options.A: That the line's voltage is no more than 50 kV
options.B: That the line is insulated
options.C: That the power line has been deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite
options.D: That a dedicated spotter has been assigned to the line

questions.explanation: Option (1) is "Deenergize and ground. Confirm from the utility owner/operator that the power line has been deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What is the first step of Option (3), Table A clearance, in 1926.1408(a)(2)(iii)(A)?

options.A: Determine the line's voltage and the minimum approach distance permitted under Table A
options.B: Measure the height of the power line above the ground
options.C: Ask OSHA to approve the planned clearance distance
options.D: Install an insulating link on the load line

questions.explanation: Option (3) starts: "(A) Determine the line's voltage and the minimum approach distance permitted under Table A".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under Option (2) of 1926.1408(a)(2), how does the employer ensure that no part of the equipment, load line or load gets closer than 20 feet to the power line?

options.A: By training each crew member under paragraph (g)
options.B: By obtaining a written clearance permit from OSHA
options.C: By implementing the measures specified in paragraph (b) of the section
options.D: By having the operator check the distance once a day

questions.explanation: Option (2) requires the employer to "Ensure that no part of the equipment, load line, or load (including rigging and lifting accessories), gets closer than 20 feet to the power line by implementing the measures specified in paragraph (b) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1408(b), the encroachment precautions apply where they are required under which options?

options.A: Option (1) only
options.B: Option (2) or Option (3)
options.C: Option (1) or Option (2)
options.D: Option (1) or Option (3)

questions.explanation: Paragraph (b) applies "Where encroachment precautions are required under Option (2) or Option (3) of this section", and then "all of the following requirements must be met".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1408(b)(3), what applies if the operator is unable to see the elevated warning line?

options.A: The warning line must be moved 10 feet closer to the equipment
options.B: Work must stop until the utility owner/operator deenergizes the line
options.C: A proximity alarm replaces the warning line and no other measure is needed
options.D: A dedicated spotter must be used, in addition to one of the measures in (b)(4)(i), (iii), (iv) and (v)

questions.explanation: "If the operator is unable to see the elevated warning line, a dedicated spotter must be used as described in § 1926.1408(b)(4)(ii) in addition to implementing one of the measures described in §§ 1926.1408(b)(4)(i), (iii), (iv) and (v)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: According to 1926.1408(b)(5), the requirements of paragraph (b)(4) do not apply to which work?

options.A: Work done under Option (3)
options.B: Work where tag lines are used
options.C: Work done during daylight hours
options.D: Work covered by subpart V of part 1926

questions.explanation: "The requirements of paragraph (b)(4) of this section do not apply to work covered by subpart V of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: During a lift the boom stays outside the minimum clearance distance, but a sling in the rigging breaches it. Does that meet the 1926.1401 definition of encroachment?

options.A: Yes; the definition covers any part of the crane, load line or load, including rigging and lifting accessories
options.B: No; only the boom and jib are counted
options.C: No; encroachment means actual contact with the power line
options.D: Only if the operator can see the power line from the cab

questions.explanation: "Encroachment is where any part of the crane, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) breaches a minimum clearance distance that this subpart requires to be maintained from a power line."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Where an insulating link/device is the measure chosen under 1926.1408(b)(4)(v), where must it be installed?

options.A: At the tip of the boom
options.B: On the power line itself
options.C: At a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load
options.D: Between the operator's cab and the boom

questions.explanation: The measure is "An insulating link/device, as defined in § 1926.1401, installed at a point between the end of the load line (or below) and the load."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Where a dedicated spotter is the measure selected under 1926.1408(b)(4)(ii), what must the spotter be equipped with?

options.A: A proximity alarm mounted on the boom tip
options.B: A visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance
options.C: A copy of the utility owner/operator's voltage records
options.D: A non-conductive tag line attached to the load

questions.explanation: The dedicated spotter must "Be equipped with a visual aid to assist in identifying the minimum clearance distance." One example the rule gives is "A clearly visible line painted on the ground".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Where Option (3) is used, what does 1926.1408(c) require of the utility owner/operator of the power lines?

options.A: Provide the requested voltage information within two working days of the employer's request
options.B: Deenergize the line within two working days of the employer's request
options.C: Send a crew to act as dedicated spotters
options.D: Mark the minimum approach distance on the ground

questions.explanation: "Where Option (3) of this section is used, the utility owner/operator of the power lines must provide the requested voltage information within two working days of the employer's request."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An employer using Option (3) must erect and maintain an elevated warning line, barricade, or line of signs in view of the operator under 1926.1408(b)(3). Where must it be placed?

options.A: Directly beneath the power line
options.B: At the edge of the equipment's maximum working radius
options.C: At a distance the operator picks from the cab
options.D: At the minimum approach distance under Table A

questions.explanation: Paragraph (b)(3) places it "at 20 feet from the power line (if using Option (2) of this section) or at the minimum approach distance under Table A (see § 1926.1408) (if using Option (3) of this section)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Using the note to Table A, a power line of exactly 200 kV falls in which voltage row?

options.A: Over 200 to 350
options.B: Up to 50
options.C: Over 50 to 200
options.D: Over 350 to 500

questions.explanation: The note says: "The value that follows “to” is up to and includes that value. For example, over 50 to 200 means up to and including 200kV."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1408(d)(1), unless an exception applies, what must the employer have confirmed before any part of the equipment, load line or load is allowed below a power line?

options.A: That a proximity alarm has been installed on the boom
options.B: That the utility owner/operator has deenergized and (at the worksite) visibly grounded the power line
options.C: That the load weighs less than the equipment's rated capacity
options.D: That the operator holds a signal person qualification

questions.explanation: Nothing is allowed below a power line "unless the employer has confirmed that the utility owner/operator has deenergized and (at the worksite) visibly grounded the power line, except where one of the exceptions in paragraph (d)(2) of this section applies."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For equipment with articulating or extensible booms, the exception in 1926.1408(d)(2)(iii) looks at the uppermost part of the equipment with the boom in which position?

options.A: Fully retracted and lowered to horizontal
options.B: At the angle planned for the lift
options.C: In the fully extended position, at true vertical
options.D: Stowed in its travel position

questions.explanation: For these booms the test is "The uppermost part of the equipment, with the boom in the fully extended position, at true vertical", compared with the plane of the power line.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Energized lines, transmitter towers and devices
questions.question: Under 1926.1408(e), the employer must assume all power lines are energized unless who confirms that the line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite?

options.A: The utility owner/operator
options.B: The crane operator
options.C: The dedicated spotter
options.D: The equipment manufacturer

questions.explanation: "The employer must assume that all power lines are energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms that the power line has been and continues to be deenergized and visibly grounded at the worksite."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1408(g)(1)(i), the training on procedures in the event of electrical contact with a power line must include what need for crew in the area?

options.A: The need to approach the equipment and help the operator climb down
options.B: The need to touch the load to check whether it is energized
options.C: The need to take over the controls from the operator
options.D: The need to avoid approaching or touching the equipment and the load

questions.explanation: The training must include "The need for crew in the area to avoid approaching or touching the equipment and the load."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1408, Power line safety (up to 350 kV)—equipment operations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1408(g)(1)(iii), power lines are presumed to be uninsulated unless who confirms that a line is insulated?

options.A: The crane operator after a visual check
options.B: The utility owner/operator or a registered engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution
options.C: Any competent person at the worksite
options.D: The equipment manufacturer

questions.explanation: "Power lines are presumed to be uninsulated unless the utility owner/operator or a registered engineer who is a qualified person with respect to electrical power transmission and distribution confirms that a line is insulated."
